main_issue: The single case directly supports the stated archive-created or pre-existing symlink-following write mechanism; physical extraction order is an important exploit precondition and is already captured by the guideline.
evidence_notes: ZIP and TAR entry handling passes attacker-controlled entry names, symlink destinations, and content streams into the shared extraction routine.
The shared routine checks lexical/canonical containment but does not prevent a normal-file write from following a target path that is already a symbolic link.
A malicious archive can place a symlink entry before a subsequent regular-file entry, causing the later write to resolve outside the extraction root.
